title: Botswana cheetahs reach Kuno
text:
Nine cheetahs from Botswana arrived at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh on February 28, 2026, adding a new international batch to Project Cheetah, the programme that is bringing the big cat back to Indian forests. Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav welcomed the animals at the park, and All India Radio carried the report the same evening. Reports at the time put India's cheetah population at 48 after the arrival, a figure that has since risen.

The move came about three months after the handover. On November 13, 2025, Botswana formally handed over eight cheetahs to India at Mokolodi Nature Reserve, near Gaborone, during the state visit of President Droupadi Murmu. The cheetahs had been brought from the Ghanzi region in the Kalahari desert. Officials from both countries briefed the two presidents at the ceremony, and the Ministry of External Affairs said the transfer was made under the next phase of Project Cheetah. President Murmu said the animals would join their relatives at Kuno National Park. Officials described the handover as a boost to wildlife cooperation between the two countries.

The nine animals were welcomed at Kuno on February 28, and Yadav released them into quarantine enclosures there. Officials said they would undergo health monitoring and acclimatisation before being moved to larger soft-release areas, and that they would not be moved into the open until that period ended. Acclimatisation gives reintroduced animals time to adjust to a new habitat and food supply before they roam freely, which is why the step is standard in translocation work. Yadav described the arrival in a social media post.

The Botswana group follows earlier batches, and the programme has relied on African partners for its animals. The cheetah had been absent from India for decades before the reintroduction began. In September 2022, eight cheetahs from an African country were released at Kuno, the first batch under the programme. A flight carrying a second batch of 12 cheetahs from South Africa took off in February 2023, and those animals were also taken to Kuno.

Kuno National Park spreads across Sheopur district in Madhya Pradesh and lies in the Gwalior Chambal region. Its core area covers about 748.76 square kilometres, and the park takes its name from the Kuno River that flows through it.

Further transfers are under discussion. Business Standard reported in September 2025 that talks were under way with Botswana, Namibia and Kenya to translocate 8 to 10 cheetahs from each country. India and Botswana had also announced a cheetah translocation pact before the November handover.

The national count has changed since February. On October 5, 2026, the birth of five cubs at Kuno was announced, taking the national total to 60.

questions.q: In which year did the Government of India officially declare the cheetah extinct in the country?
questions.explanation: The cheetah was officially declared extinct in India in 1952. The passage refers to the species only as having been absent for decades, so the year must come from outside the passage.

list1: I. Range of the Asiatic cheetah subspecies
II. IUCN Red List status of the cheetah species
III. IUCN Red List status of the Asiatic cheetah subspecies
IV. Mature cheetah individuals estimated by the IUCN (2021 assessment)
questions.explanation: The Asiatic cheetah (A. j. venaticus) is found in Iran and is rated Critically Endangered by the IUCN. The cheetah species as a whole is rated Vulnerable, with an estimated 6,517 mature individuals in the 2021 assessment.

questions.assertion: India's cheetah reintroduction has relied on batches brought from more than one African country.
questions.reason: The first batch of cheetahs brought to India for Project Cheetah came from Namibia in 2022.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: batches came from Namibia, South Africa and Botswana. The Namibian origin of the first batch is not a reason for the reliance on several countries, so R is true but does not explain A.

statements: I. The Asiatic cheetah subspecies is rated Critically Endangered by the IUCN.
II. The cheetah species as a whole is rated Least Concern by the IUCN.
questions.explanation: Statement I is true (Asiatic cheetah, Iran, Critically Endangered). Statement II is false: the cheetah species is rated Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.

statements: 1. Kuno was notified as a national park in 2018, having earlier been a wildlife sanctuary.
2. Kuno was identified in the 1990s as a possible site for reintroducing the Asiatic lion to establish a second population outside Gujarat.
3. In April 2025, two South African cheetahs, Prabhas and Pavak, were moved from Kuno to Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary.
4. The Kuno River, after which the park is named, is a tributary of the Narmada River.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Kuno River is a tributary of the Chambal, not the Narmada. Three statements are correct, so the answer is Only three.
